parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عقیق, borrowed form Arabic عَقِيق (ʕaqīq), borrowed from Aramaic עקיק.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish باب (bâb), borrowed from Arabic بَاب (bāb), borrowed from Aramaic בָּבָא, borrowed from Akkadian bābum.

From Ottoman Turkish دفتر (defter), from Arabic دَفْتَر (daftar), from Aramaic דהפתּיר (defter), from Ancient Greek διφθέρα (diphthéra). Old Turkic [Term?] (/⁠tepter⁠/) is an early borrowing from Aramaic or Middle Persian. https://www.etimolojiturkce.com/kelime/defter

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دكان (düḱḱan), from Arabic دُكَّان (dukkān), from Aramaic דּוּכָּנָא (dukkānā, “dais”), from Akkadian 𒆠𒍇 (/⁠dakkannu⁠/, “dais, platform, bench; niche, bedroom, private chambers or quarters”), from Sumerian 𒆠𒍇 (/⁠daggan⁠/, “chamber, doorway or its frame, niche in a wall
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خرنوب (harnub), from Arabic خَرْنُوب (ḵarnūb), variant of خَرُّوب (ḵarrūb, “carob”), ultimately from Aramaic חַרּוּבָא (ḥarrūḇā, “carob”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish حلزون (halezon, halezun), from Arabic حَلَزُون (ḥalazūn), from Aramaic חְלָזוֹנָא / ܚܠܵܙܘܿܢܵܐ (ḥəlāzōnā, “snail”).

parole.significato: endive, any leafy salad vegetable of the species Cichorium endivia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish هندبا (hindiba), from Arabic هِنْدِبَاء (hindibāʔ), ultimately from Aramaic הּנְדְּבָא (hendǝḇā).

parole.significato: cardamom, a perennial plant of the species Elettaria cardamomum, native to southern India
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قاقله (kakule), from Arabic قَاقُلَّة (qāqulla, “seepweed; various types of spices”), from Aramaic קָקוּלָא (qāqullā).
From Ottoman Turkish كبریت (kibrit), from Arabic كِبْرِيت (kibrīt), from Aramaic כִּבְּרִיתָא (kiḇrīṯā), from Akkadian 𒆠𒀀𒀭𒀀𒇉 (kibrītu, “sulfur, firebrand”).

parole.significato: cumin, a flowering plant of the species Cuminum cyminum and its aromatic seed
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كمیون (kimyon), from Arabic كَمُّون (kammūn), from Aramaic כַּמֹּונָֹא / ܩܰܡܽܘܢܳܐ (kammōnā, “cumin”), from Akkadian 𒌑𒁷𒊺𒉪 (Ú.GAMUN /⁠kamūnu⁠/, “cumin”), from Sumerian [Term?] (/⁠gamun⁠/, “cumin”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قربان (kurban), borrowed from Arabic قُرْبَان (qurbān), borrowed from Aramaic קורבנא (qurbānā).

parole.significato: The first two months of winter
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كانون (kânûn, “hearth; first two months of winter”), from Arabic كَانُون (kānūn, “hearth”), from Aramaic כָּנוֹנָא / ܟܢܘܢܐ (kānōnā, “brazier”), from Akkadian 𒆠𒉈 (KI.NE /⁠kanūnu⁠/, “brazier, kiln, stove, hearth; a name of a ritual and also the month it takes place”).

parole.significato: an adherent of Zoroastrianism, a Magian
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مجوسی, from Arabic مَجُوسِيّ (majūsiyy), from Aramaic 𐡌𐡂𐡅𐡔 (mgwš), from Old Persian 𐎶𐎦𐏁 (m-gu-š /⁠maguš⁠/).
From Ottoman Turkish نغمه, from Arabic نَغْمة (naḡma, “melody, tone, sound”), from Aramaic ܢܥܡܬܐ (nāˁamtā, “melody, sweet and soft voice”), from Hebrew נעם (nāˁam, “sweet singing”).
From Ottoman Turkish پطریق, from Arabic بِطْرِيق (biṭrīq) from Aramaic פטריק / ܦܛܪܝܩ (/⁠paṭrīq⁠/), from Ancient Greek πατρίκιος (patríkios), from Latin pātricius.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پلیت (pelit, “acorn”), from Arabic بلّوط (ballūṭ, “oak; acorn”), ultimately from Aramaic בְּלוּטָא (bəllūṭā, ballūṭā, “oak; acorn”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صندوق (sandık), borrowed from Arabic صَنْدُوق (ṣandūq), borrowed from Aramaic צנדוק (ṣəndūq, “coffer, especially one storing documents, safe-guarding precious items”), borrowed from Ancient Greek σῠνθήκη (sŭnthḗkē), from σῠντῐ́θημῐ (sŭntĭ́thēmĭ, “to place or put togeth
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سمت (semt), from Arabic سَمْت (samt), from Aramaic סֵימִטָא (sēmiṭā) from Latin sēmĭta.

parole.significato: coin die, any of the metal stamps used to strike impressions of designs onto coins
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سكه (sikke, “coin die; coin; kind of cap”) from Arabic سِكَّة (sikka, “coin die; coin”), from Aramaic סִכְּתָא (sekkǝṯā, “peg, nail, spike; ploughshare; coin stamp”), ultimately from Akkadian 𒄑𒆕 (sikkatum, “peg, nail; cone, pyramid”).

parole.significato: A monarchic title for Sunni Muslim monarchs.
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish سلطان (sultân), from Arabic سُلْطَان (sulṭān), from Aramaic שולטנא (šulṭānā, “strength, authority”) (compare Hebrew שִׁלְטוֹן (shiltón)).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طاووس, from Old Anatolian Turkish طاووس, from Arabic طَاوُوس (ṭāwūs), Aramaic טַוסָא (ṭawsā), from Ancient Greek τᾰώς (tăṓs). Compare Persian طاووس.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یهودی (yahudî), borrowed from Arabic يَهُودِيّ (yahūdiyy), borrowed from Aramaic יְהוּדָיֵא (yəhūḏāyā). Doublet of Çıfıt.

parole.significato: zaatar, a particular herb of the species Origanum syriacum and the seasoning made thereof
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زعتر (zaʼter), from Arabic زَعْتَر (zaʕtar, “zaatar, wild thyme”), assumed to be from Aramaic צתרא (ṣaṯrā, ṣāṯrā).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish عالم (alem), borrowed from Arabic عَالَم (ʕālam), borrowed from Aramaic עָלְמָא / ܥܳܠܡܳܐ (ʿāləmā).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسطوانه, استوانه, from Arabic أُسْطُوَانَة (ʔusṭuwāna), from Aramaic אִיסְטְוָונָא (ʾesṭwānā, “column, pillar”) ultimately from Middle Persian [script needed] (stwn' /⁠stūn⁠/, “column, pillar”). Doublet of sütun, derived from New Persian.

parole.significato: waterfall, falls, cascade, cataract, a flow of water over the edge of a cliff
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شلاله (şelale), from Arabic شَلَّالَة (šallāla), variant of شَلَّال (šallāl, “waterfall”), a word of Aramaic origin.
